text:
There will be a Beast. There will be an image. There will be demanded worship. There will be a mark connected to his name and number. There will be commercial exclusion for those who refuse. The Bible believer does not need to panic before those elements exist. He needs to read the Book.

Chapter Six — The Price of the Beast’s Bread Is the Wrath of God

If Revelation 13 shows the pressure to receive the mark, Revelation 14 shows what God thinks of receiving it. The third angel follows the announcement of Babylon’s fall and declares “with a loud voice” that if any man worships the Beast and his image and receives his mark, “The same shall drink of the wine of the wrath of God, which is poured out without mixture into the cup of his indignation” (Revelation 14:9–10). That is not corrective discipline. It is divine wrath. The Beast promises participation in his system. God announces the final price.

The language gets harder, not softer: “he shall be tormented with fire and brimstone in the presence of the holy angels, and in the presence of the Lamb” (Revelation 14:10). Then: “the smoke of their torment ascendeth up for ever and ever” and “they have no rest day nor night” (Revelation 14:11). Modern religion may sand the edges off judgment until hell sounds like a temporary counseling session, but Revelation refuses to cooperate. The Beast offers temporary bread and permanent ruin. He offers access to the market and exclusion from God’s mercy. He offers survival for the afternoon and judgment without end. That is the devil’s bargain: he always gives a man something that expires in exchange for something that does not.

Then comes Revelation 14:12: “Here is the patience of the saints: here are they that keep the commandments of God, and the faith of Jesus.” Now the context gives “patience” its proper weight. These saints are not enduring somebody making fun of their Bible at the office. They are enduring a world order that attaches survival to apostasy. They refuse the Beast when refusal can cost food, business, liberty, and life. Revelation 20:4 later shows people beheaded because they “had not worshipped the beast, neither his image, neither had received his mark.” Their endurance is not a church-age formula for maintaining justification by good behavior. It is faithfulness under a prophetic system where the Beast places the price tag of compromise on ordinary human survival.

Chapter Seven — Do Not Drag the Beast’s Mark Back Into the Body of Christ

Here is where right division saves a man from theological indigestion. The Body of Christ has its own doctrine, position, promises, calling, and destiny. Paul says of the believer, “after that ye believed, ye were sealed with that holy Spirit of promise” (Ephesians 1:13). He then calls the Holy Spirit “the earnest of our inheritance until the redemption of the purchased possession” (Ephesians 1:14). Later he commands believers, “grieve not the holy Spirit of God, whereby ye are sealed unto the day of redemption” (Ephesians 4:30). That is not a temporary probationary sticker. God did not say the believer is sealed until the next government program frightens him.

text:
Nigeria Arrests Chinese Nationals in Illegal Fishing Crackdown

The three-day joint fisheries operation intercepted three vessels

The Nigerian Navy and Federal Department of Fisheries and Aquaculture (FDFA) arrested 33 people, including three Chinese nationals, in late August as part of a three-day initiative known as Exercise Coastal Grip II and Operation Abo Eja.

It was not immediately clear what the Chinese nationals did on the vessels, but Chinese fishing captains have committed illegal, unregulated and unreported (IUU) fishing in the Gulf of Guinea for decades. Also arrested were two Ghanaians and 28 Nigerians. Chinese captains routinely hire African workers.

The operation involved naval ships, helicopters, Special Boat Service personnel and maritime surveillance assets, and was coordinated through the Western Naval Command Mission Control Centre, Nigeria’s Channels Television reported. Fisheries officials offered technical guidance.

“The Operation has demonstrated the importance of maintaining a strong presence at sea, as regular and credible surveillance creates deterrent and encourages compliance amongst the legitimate operators and provides the authorities with valuable information on the activities taking place on the Nigerian maritime jurisdictions,” Adeleke Adegoke, FDFA deputy director, said in a Radio Nigeria report.

After the arrests, Nigerian Navy Rear Adm. Abubakar Mustapha told reporters that IUU fishing has reduced the country’s fish stocks to the extent that it now imports more than 70% of its “fishery needs.”

“So, the partnership between the Nigerian Navy and the [FDFA] is a step in the right direction,” Mustapha said in a Channels Television report. “In fact, the days of illegal fishers and poachers are numbered because the intersection of security, which the Navy brings, and regulation, which the [FDFA] brings to the table, would translate to the denial of these criminal activities, and which will also translate to more revenue and more food security.”

Nigeria loses about $70 million annually to illegal fishing perpetrated by a host of foreign fleets. Beijing commands the world’s largest distant-water fishing fleet and is the world’s worst illegal fishing offender, according to the IUU Fishing Risk Index. Due mostly to illegal Chinese fishing vessels, West Africa has become the world’s epicenter for IUU fishing. It costs the region an estimated $10 billion a year, according to a Stimson Center think tank report.

Chinese vessels commit many fishing violations, including bottom trawling, which involves dragging a net along the sea floor, indiscriminately scooping up marine life. This kills juvenile fish, decimates fish stocks and destroys ecosystems.

Beijing’s vessels also commonly fish illegally in countries’ exclusive economic zones and abuse local rules to enter African fishing registries under local flags. This is known as flagging in, or flying a flag of convenience. It helps a vessel’s owners dodge financial charges and other regulations.

Beijing recently refused to sign the Mombasa Declaration, an agreement meant to improve efforts to combat illegal fishing in East Africa. Steve Trent, CEO and co-founder of the Environmental Justice Foundation, said the Chinese government has taken a disingenuous approach regarding its fishing fleet.

“It’s simply not credible for them to carry on in this way,” Trent told the BBC in July. “China, to date, still is not doing nearly enough to control its fleet. In fact, I would say they’re enabling it, through subsidies, through a lack of oversight and control.”

Nigeria and other West African nations are collaborating to halt illegal fishing. On June 1, the Combined Maritime Task Force (CMTF) was established to address IUU fishing and other regional sea crimes. Côte d’Ivoire, The Gambia, Ghana, Liberia and Sierra Leone joined Nigeria in signing the pact. The CMTF will be the first joint, African-led maritime security effort to include a rapid response force

text:
The Eucharistic theology of the Assyrian Church of the East cannot plausibly be treated as an anticipation of classical Reformed views of the same. The resemblance sometimes rests upon reading East-Syriac words such as “type,” “symbol,” or “memorial” through categories they did not originally carry.

In the East-Syriac tradition, a type need not be an absent sign pointing toward a distant reality. It can sacramentally participate in the mystery it signifies. An ACOE theological treatment explicitly warns against confusing “type” with mere symbol: the type “may indeed participate in the ‘mystery’ (rāzā) to which it points.”

https://t.co/u5qZz5GPyL

More importantly, the ACOE’s own contemporary doctrinal statements are remarkably concrete. Its official Australian diocesan exposition says that through Christ’s command “the bread is changed into His Holy Body, and the wine into His Precious Blood”; communicants encounter Christ Himself and are united to Him through His Body and Blood.

https://t.co/HUOJUAQjra

The ACOE Diocese of California likewise states simply that the Eucharist “is the true Body and Blood of our Lord Jesus Christ.”

https://t.co/shpoeiCHjx

The 2017 Catholic–Assyrian Common Statement on Sacramental Life makes the point even more explicitly: through the Eucharistic prayer the bread and wine “sacramentally become the Body and Blood of our Lord,” while Christ’s “real and true presence” under the species of bread and wine belongs to their common faith.

https://t.co/crI69XiikP

Nor is the Eucharist merely a congregational commemoration. The ancient East-Syriac Qurbana is an offering, celebrated by an ordained priest within an apostolic-sacramental ecclesiology.

https://t.co/k0GPBwOUrO

In 2001 the Catholic Church, following dialogue with the ACOE, formally recognized that it had preserved “full Eucharistic faith” both in Christ’s presence under bread and wine and in the sacrificial character of the Eucharist.

https://t.co/kiZZLGuqNL

None of the foregoing requires pretending that East-Syriac theology simply reproduces medieval Latin transubstantiation. It does not. Its vocabulary, conceptual apparatus, and liturgical emphases are distinct.

But distinct from scholastic Latin theology does not mean, in this case, proto-Reformed.

The historical ACOE framework is sacerdotal, sacrificial, realist, sacramental and episcopal: an ordained priest offers the Qurbana; bread and wine sacramentally become Christ’s Body and Blood; Christ is really and truly present; and communion objectively communicates participation in the sacred mystery.

Whatever legitimate differences remain among the ancient apostolic traditions concerning the precise explanation of Eucharistic presence, the conceptual world of the Church of the East belongs unmistakably to that ancient sacramental universe.

Reading it as a precursor of classical Reformed Eucharistic theology is anachronistic.

Mandatory Accommodations: The California Fair Employment and Housing Act requires employers of five or more employees to provide reasonable accommodation for individuals with physical or mental disabilities. This accommodation is required to help employees apply for jobs and perform essential job functions, unless it would cause an undue hardship.

The Interactive Process: Employers are required to initiate an "interactive process" when an employee requests reasonable accommodations. Additionally, the employer must offer to initiate this process when they become aware of a possible need for an accommodation. This awareness might come through a third party, observation, or because the employee has exhausted leave benefits but still needs accommodation.

Good Faith Requirement: In California, it is unlawful for an employer to fail to engage in a timely, good faith, interactive process. The entire point of this process is to remove barriers that keep people from performing jobs that they could do with some form of accommodation.

Individualized Assessment: The interactive process requires an individualized assessment. This assessment must evaluate both the job itself and the specific physical or mental limitations of the individual that directly relate to the need for accommodation.

Types of Reasonable Accommodations: According to the text, accommodations that may have been relevant to your situation include changing job duties, providing leave for medical care, or changing work schedules. Other listed examples include relocating the work area or providing mechanical or electrical aids.

As far as what has been announced so far, the reported proposal for a Production Tax Credit-based Federal Program cannot help to build anything in the country. However, our Universal Federal Film Tax Credit Bill can provide this for everyone!

In the earliest drafts of our Universal Federal Bill, we included our "Babs Do Studios Infrastructure Plan" to provide nationwide studio infrastructure so that every state could quickly and economically have the necessary production, business, and training infrastructure to support nationwide Film & Media production and business development. 

However, as we campaigned for our State-level Universal Bills, it became clear that some states will require more time for policy and business development than others and to make our Universal Bills truly "Universal", their benefits and solutions should be for everyone. So, we took the stance of planning for states that will work for our development and productions and give more opportunities to other artists, builders, and entrepreneurs to come up with their own studio businesses through the program.

Yet, as we have only heard about Production Tax Credits being considered for the Federal Film Tax Credit Program instead of adding Infrastructure Tax Credits to help the country to build, we want to inform you of our "Babs Do Studios Infrastructure Plan" and why it isn't in the current draft of our Universal Federal Film Tax Credit Bill. Because, if Infrastructure Tax Credits or some other simple financing solutions aren't put in place, nobody can afford to build such high-cost infrastructure and the amount of people with the technical knowledge, business interest, and creative drive to plan out and for building a film studio are so limited that states could continue to go decades without competitive infrastructure waiting for someone to come in and build a single film studio. 

This is exactly what we have faced in Nevada, the "Entertainment Capital of the World", with an outdated $10M Film Tax Credit Program that no one will invest the time, money, and effort to build a film studio in. Babs Do Studios was designed to solve this with our economical and quick to build design and we have directly missed out on two $100M+ film studio deals because the Nevada Film Tax Credit Program is too small. That's why we are campaigning for our $125M Universal Film Tax Credit Bill for Nevada with its own Production and Infrastructure Tax Credits that will allow for even larger development opportunities when combined with our Universal Federal Film Tax Credit Bill Program!

Paramount/WBD needed infrastructure, it's not there and will have to be built to support them, if not in the next few years then at some point. If it requires us to step up and offer our Babs Do Studios Infrastructure Plan as well as our Universal Federal Film Tax Credit Bill, with the cooperation of the President and members of Congress to secure this national investment in Film & Media business, infrastructure, and industry development we can make that happen either by contract or by re-incorporation into a new draft of our Universal Federal Film Tax Credit Bill to benefit every Artist, Student, and Worker in Film & Media across the United States. 

As it is, our Universal Federal Film Tax Credit Bill provides the innovations and solutions the U.S. Entertainment Industry needs to be revitalized and advanced by decades for larger and more widespread production and industry development. As events in the industry continue to happen on an almost daily basis with worries of further decline and various group efforts to find solutions to prevent it, we ask for your support to bring forward our Universal Federal Film Tax Credit Bill to serve as the base legislation, in whole or in part, of the "Motion Picture, Television, and Entertainment Revitalization Act" in order to truly revitalize and, in many cases, revolutionize the U.S. Entertainment Industry for all!

text:
It is time to listen, @realDonaldTrump @POTUS & @JonVoight @TheSlyStallone @LauraFriedmanCA @RepLindaSanchez @RepBrianJack @RepNateMoran understand, Paramount/WBD have reportedly shared concerns about the lack of infrastructure in their search for a new state to relocate their studios to and now even just their offices which they are seeking a 400,000 sq ft office.

A Federal Film Tax Incentive Program based solely on just providing Production Tax Credits will do nothing to help build infrastructure, business, or industry. They literally can't be used for this purpose. So, if a state doesn't have the infrastructure, supporting businesses, and professional training solutions in place, adding a Film Tax Incentive Program won't do anything if nobody has the spaces or resources to film something in the state. 

We have 50 states and a "Big Five" studio system that can barely make a handful of movies a year, especially with overblown Hollywood budgets, and with many being shot on backlots and Virtual Production LED screen stages. Even worse, many productions are already in Canada or moved overseas to Europe and other countries with additional outsourcing to foreign countries for VFX, Animation, and Post-Production. A basic layer of Production Tax Credits will not lure these productions back to the U.S. so why would we throw Billions at trying to bring their business back instead of building up new "Hollywood 2.0" studios with new U.S.-based productions?

Our Universal Federal Film Tax Credit Bill solves this problem for infrastructure and new business development with Infrastructure Tax Credits alongside Production Tax Credits. States will finally have the means to provide artists and developers support for building high-cost Film & Media infrastructure in their states which will contribute to the local generation of production jobs to increase economic impact in their state. This would also incentivize the state to boost its State-level Film Tax Credit Program, if it even had one to begin with, in order to further benefit from this new industry and economic generator.

Furthermore, with factors such as the overblown costs of Hollywood production, the failing of Streaming market economics, and with AI investment dominating investor dollars, there's not much traditional market money to go around for investing in Film & Media. Reports are that Hollywood has been having to cut production numbers and not greenlight anything because of this loss of basic funding solutions. If they can't finance their projects, independent filmmakers certainly can't and no matter the spin for "brand marketing", "creator economy", "vertical media" or any other useless media article trend, real work can't be done with everyone barely scraping by. To answer this, our Universal Federal Film Tax Credit Bill provides much needed innovations and solutions to simplify investment and financing for Film & Media production and infrastructure projects. Citizens, companies, banks, and local governments will be able to invest and finance projects like never before with common sense methods and standards to secure local development and major production alike.

With other measures such as program protections against foreign production flight, outsourcing, the National Film Fund, and others, our Universal Federal Film Tax Credit Program goes even further to solve these and other issues. At the same time we are campaigning for our State-level Universal Film Tax Credit Bill here in Nevada to greatly upgrade the state's outdated $10M Program with a new $125M Program with Production and Infrastructure Tax Credits that would pair perfectly with our Universal Federal Bill. 

This, we believe is the disconnect with the currently reported Production Tax Credit Federal Program, there's no connection with the needs of the Film & Media industry or the states that will be included in the program. As with Paramount/WBD's concerns, there's clearly no perspective for the needs of film studio development or even the thought for Film & Media infrastructure development at all. It's all just for Production Tax Credits which were never the real problem as states can increase their Production Tax Credits as much as they want but they currently can't build local industry even if they wanted to right now. 

A Federal Program must do more and solve more than a State Program can and in terms of our Universal Bills, we can campaign for multiple states to adopt our innovative Bills but with 50 states and mixed levels of politics and legislative session years, it will take far longer to go state to state than to pass our Universal Federal Bill which would help advance the entire U.S. Entertainment Industry overnight while we work to upgrade state programs over the next several years.

If it is true that a Federal Film Tax Credit Bill proposal is announced next week, it must do more than just uselessly throwing  Production Tax Credits at the problem. We ask that, if anything, that you consider putting forward our Universal Federal Film Tax Credit Bill, in whole or even in part, to serve as the base legislation for the "Motion Picture, Television, and Entertainment Revitalization Act". We are filmmakers, we have been working to build our own film studio development, we have talked with economic development departments and film offices across the country, we have discussed with studio developers and companies that own film studios or have been foreclosed on, we're not random nobodies on the internet and as our government representatives, we ask you to please listen, understand, and recognize our point of view on this matter as by just being drafters of legislation at the State and Federal level, it is clear that our perspective is immediately far more relevant and comprehensive than most.

The latest draft of our Universal Federal Film Tax Credit Bill is pinned to our page here on X and is posted on our Babs Do Studios Blog. We have also submitted the latest draft of our Universal Federal Bill to most of your staff as well. If refinements, discussions, and more need to happen, let's work together to establish this historic legislation as soon as possible to provide for and benefit the future of U.S. Entertainment for all!

text:
A fence sitting 7 inches onto your lot is an encroachment.

You could lose those 7 inches by adverse possession (sometimes called “squatter’s rights”) and can eventually transfer title to the other property owner.

Conditions must be met for you to lose that part of your property.
1) The use must be open, obvious, exclusive, continuous, and without your permission.
2) It must last the full statutory period in your state so check your state and determine the length, which can be from 5 to 21 years. California is the shortest at 5 years).
3) After enough years of silence some states recognize “boundary by acquiescence” or an implied agreement that the fence is the line.
4) In a lot of states the neighbor also has to pay property taxes on the disputed strip.

This last item is where most claims of a few inches fail.

Where the real headache comes is if you decide to sell your house. A new survey will show the fence inside your legal description. Buyers, lenders, and title companies often treat that as a defect. You may have to move the fence, get a boundary-line agreement, or take a price cut.

So what should you do.

a) Get a licensed survey so you have official measurements, not just a tape measure.
b) Send a polite but written notice (certified mail) pointing out the encroachment and asking them to move the fence.
c) If they refuse, a short letter from a real-estate attorney often works. You can also offer a written license (“you may keep the fence there for $1 a year”) which kills the “hostile” element required for adverse possession.

St. Michael’s Abbey is a monastery of the Norbertine Fathers located in Silverado Canyon, Orange County, California.

Founded in 1961 by seven Hungarian priests escaping communist persecution, the abbey combines contemplative community life with active priestly ministry, such as teaching, parish work, and chaplaincies.

The Norbertines gather several times each day to chant the psalms, antiphons, and prayers in Latin using Gregorian chant. The noon office offers a brief pause in the working day to redirect the mind to prayer, commemorating the hour of Christ’s crucifixion.
